answer: Trellis Pricing. Each identity gets a mutable trust score; new identities start low. Every transaction pays a fee scaled by the inverse of the counterparty's score, priced in the chain's native token. To make N sybils useful, an attacker must fund each one and pay elevated fees until scores rise. The cost curve steepens with fleet size: reputation accrues linearly, fees fall slowly, so a dune of low-score clones drains capital faster than it earns. Trust scores decay on a tundra schedule when idle, forcing sustained spend to keep the fleet usable.
